investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" when the eval runner calls POST /api/agents. The eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent swarm quota, so no new remote agent can be created. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (evidenced by run-status-probes.mjs line 1339 calling createAgent immediately after requireOrgId), every downstream check in the feature fails with the same message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Fails with SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api and STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT on desktop-release
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed on both the production-api and desktop-release runtime environments. On production-api, the stream terminated immediately (latencyMs=1980) with a generation_error frame carrying error code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and the message "agent runtime endpoint not found (404)", indicating the agent runtime harness is unreachable or misconfigured at the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint. On desktop-release, the stream emitted multiple generation_progress frames but then timed out after 120 seconds with STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT, never producing a generation_completed frame or an image URL artifact. Both failures are eval-layer failures; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The agent runtime harness backing the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint is unreachable (HTTP 404) in the production-api environment, causing an immediate SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error before any image generation can proceed. In the desktop-release environment the harness is reachable and begins generating (multiple generation_progress frames observed) but the upstream image generation pipeline stalls and never emits a generation_completed frame or image URL within the 120-second eval window, resulting in a STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT. The two failures have distinct proximate causes (harness 404 vs. upstream generation stall) but share the same downstream contract violation: neither environment produced the required generation_completed frame type or a non-false imageUrlPresent value as mandated by the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 271-272.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Terminates with STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT Before Emitting generation_completed or Artifact URL
investigations.summary: The desktop-release eval for image-generation-stream failed because the upstream SSE endpoint /api/generate/image/stream stalled after emitting only generation_progress frames and then terminated with a STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT error (code: STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT, "upstream stream produced no data for 120s") instead of a generation_completed frame and an artifact URL. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent === true — were violated, confirming the upstream image generation backend did not complete within the eval window.
investigations.rootCause: The upstream image generation service behind /api/generate/image/stream stopped producing SSE data after reaching approximately 10% progress, held the connection idle for 120 seconds, and then the eval harness closed the stream with a STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT sentinel event. The stream never emitted a generation_completed frame nor an artifact URL, causing both contract assertions to fail. This is localized to the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint in the desktop-release runtime environment; no evidence of a user-facing production outage is present in the packet. The production-api sibling check failed for a separate, independent reason (404 harness unreachable), so the two failures are not correlated to a shared dependency.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: POST /api/agents Returns 409 Agent Quota Exceeded (limit is 100)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-16T03:59:58Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached for the eval org. Because the agent creation call is rejected before any agent is provisioned, zero required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) were collected, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" when the eval runner calls POST /api/agents. The eval org has reached or exceeded the 100-agent swarm quota, so no new remote agent can be created. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (evidenced by run-status-probes.mjs line 1339 calling createAgent immediately after requireOrgId), every downstream check in the feature fails with the same message. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

Prior eval runs may have created agents that were not cleaned up (withCleanup in the runner may have failed silently or been interrupted), causing agents to accumulate until the quota was exhausted.

[Medium confidence] A previous eval run crashed or was cancelled before the withCleanup callback could delete the provisioned agent, leaving a leaked agent in the org. Repeated occurrences over time would fill the quota.
[Lower confidence] The quota limit of 100 was recently lowered on the swarm backend for the eval org, causing previously-passing runs to now exceed the limit.

investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed on both the production-api and desktop-release runtime environments. On desktop-release, the stream emitted multiple generation_progress frames but then timed out after 120 seconds with STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT, never producing a generation_completed frame or an image URL artifact. Both failures are eval-layer failures; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
